section: Soil, noise, thermal, marine and radioactive pollution - sources, effects and control
subsections: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash
Thermal pollution - sources, effect on DO

accepted.s: Which one of the following best defines soil pollution?
o: A natural increase in soil fertility due to crop rotation
A temporary rise in soil moisture caused by irrigation
A reduction in soil temperature caused by afforestation
A build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil
accepted.x: Soil pollution is the build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil.
accepted.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a related environmental effect.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of soil pollution:
1. Floods, acid rain and mineral deposition from weathered rock are natural causes.
2. Industrial waste, farm runoff and urban waste are human causes.
3. Mining, e-waste and coal ash can contribute to soil pollution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Floods, acid rain and mineral deposition are natural causes, while industrial waste, farm runoff, urban waste, mining, e-waste and coal ash are human causes of soil pollution.
accepted.tq: Combine natural and human causes and identify the inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Heavy metal)
a. Mercury
b. Cadmium
c. Copper, zinc and lead
 d. Chromates

List-II (Major source)
i. Tanneries and industrial waste
 ii. Mining effluent, phosphate fertilisers and batteries
 iii. Industrial effluent from chlor-alkali industries and fungicides
 iv. Smelting and industrial waste

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Mercury is associated with chlor-alkali effluent and fungicides; cadmium with mining effluent, phosphate fertilisers and batteries; copper, zinc and lead with smelting and industrial waste; and chromates with tanneries and industrial waste.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure heavy-metal and source pair.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following diseases is associated with mercury pollution?
accepted.x: Mercury pollution is associated with Minamata disease, whereas cadmium pollution is associated with itai-itai disease.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two heavy-metal disease associations.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Itai-itai disease is particularly associated with contamination by which heavy metal?
accepted.x: Cadmium contamination, arising among other sources from mining effluent, phosphate fertilisers and batteries, is associated with itai-itai disease.
accepted.tq: Test the commonly confused heavy-metal disease pair.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about DDT:
1. It is a persistent organic pollutant.
2. It resists breakdown in the environment.
3. It biomagnifies through food chains.
4. It is listed under the Stockholm Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: DDT is a persistent organic pollutant, resists breakdown, biomagnifies up food chains and is listed under the Stockholm Convention.
accepted.tq: Recognise that all four statements describe the same pollutant accurately.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The requirement that fly ash be used in bricks, cement and roads within what distance of thermal power plants is intended to prevent its dumping on soil?
accepted.x: MoEFCC requires fly ash to be used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants, thereby discouraging its dumping on soil.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific regulatory distance and reject altered ranges.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Contaminated Sites Rules, consider the following statements:
1. They are made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. Sites are tested against 189 hazardous chemicals.
3. The Polluter Pays principle applies to them.
4. Radioactive waste is covered without exemption.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Rules operate under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, test sites against 189 hazardous chemicals and apply the Polluter Pays principle. Radioactive waste is exempt.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the stated exemption.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT exempt from the scope of the Contaminated Sites Rules?
accepted.x: The Rules cover identification and remediation of chemically contaminated sites. Radioactive waste, mining, marine oil pollution and dumpsites are exempt.
accepted.tq: Find the item that belongs within the Rules rather than among their exemptions.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules, what proportion of the fund is kept by the Centre?
accepted.x: Twenty-five per cent of the Environment (Protection) Fund is kept by the Centre; the money may be used for soil-pollution control and site remediation.
accepted.tq: Recall the percentage rather than confusing it with the larger residual share.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations consists entirely of measures for controlling soil pollution?
1. Use of biofertilisers and integrated pest management
2. Afforestation and scientific disposal of waste
3. Biomining of legacy dumps and reduced use of chemical fertilisers
4. Increasing pesticide use and indiscriminate dumping
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Biofertilisers, integrated pest management, afforestation, scientific waste disposal, biomining and reduced chemical inputs are control measures. Increasing pesticide use and indiscriminate dumping are not.
accepted.tq: Separate genuine control measures from the reversed harmful practice.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated effect of soil pollution?
o: Increase in soil biodiversity in all conditions
accepted.x: Soil pollution may reduce vegetation, disturb soil fauna, produce toxic crops, clog drains and cause foul smell. It does not necessarily increase soil biodiversity.
accepted.tq: Identify the exaggerated reversal of an environmental effect.
accepted.sec: Soil pollution - control, heavy metals → sources, DDT, fly ash  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the agent used in bioremediation?
o: Biostimulation — removal of all native microbes
Mycoremediation — addition of chemical fertilisers only
accepted.x: Bioaugmentation involves adding pollutant-degrading microbes. Phytoremediation uses plants, biostimulation adds nutrients to native microbes, and mycoremediation uses fungi.
accepted.tq: Use the agent-based distinction among closely named techniques.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation and green technologies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In biostimulation, the principal intervention is to:
o: Add nutrients to boost native microbes
Replace all native microbes with engineered plants
Add fungi to absorb heavy metals
Burn contaminated soil at high temperature
accepted.x: Biostimulation means adding nutrients to stimulate the activity of native pollutant-degrading microbes.
accepted.tq: Apply the meaning of the process name to the intervention described.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation and green technologies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mycoremediation is bioremediation carried out with the help of:
accepted.x: Mycoremediation uses fungi to assist in the remediation of pollutants.
accepted.tq: Break the technical term into its biological agent.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation and green technologies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a limitation of bioremediation?
o: It is necessarily more expensive than every conventional method.
Its results do not vary with environmental conditions.
It is always faster than chemical treatment.
It may be slower than chemical treatment and its results vary with conditions.
accepted.x: Bioremediation is eco-friendly and cheaper, but it can be slower than chemical treatment and its results vary with environmental conditions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish advantages from limitations without accepting absolute claims.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation and green technologies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Oil Zapper, developed from a consortium of bacteria associated with TERI, is used primarily to:
o: Degrade oily sludge and crude from oil spills
Increase dissolved oxygen in thermal effluents
Remove radioactive materials from mining sites
accepted.x: Oil Zapper is a consortium of bacteria from TERI that consumes oily sludge and crude oil from oil spills.
accepted.tq: Match the named technology with its specific environmental application.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation and green technologies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's first Dark Sky Reserve was established at:
accepted.x: India's first Dark Sky Reserve is at Hanle, Ladakh, established in 2022 within Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first Dark Sky Reserve and the first Dark Sky Park.
accepted.sec: Light pollution - dark sky reserves  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's designated dark-sky locations:
1. Hanle became India's first Dark Sky Reserve in 2022.
2. Hanle lies inside Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary.
3. Pench Tiger Reserve became India's first Dark Sky Park in 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Hanle in Ladakh became India's first Dark Sky Reserve in 2022 within Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, while Pench Tiger Reserve became India's first Dark Sky Park in 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate the reserve, sanctuary and park facts while retaining the dates.
accepted.sec: Light pollution - dark sky reserves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion associated with a dark sky reserve?
o: A protected core with a buffer zone
accepted.x: Dark sky reserves require very little artificial light, clear and dry skies, a protected core with a buffer and community light-management rules. Unrestricted high-intensity lighting is contrary to these criteria.
accepted.tq: Identify the practice that contradicts the defining criteria.
accepted.sec: Light pollution - dark sky reserves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation certifies dark sky reserves?
accepted.x: Certification of dark sky reserves is provided by DarkSky International.
accepted.tq: Use the exact certifying body rather than a similarly international organisation.
accepted.sec: Light pollution - dark sky reserves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Hanle is considered suitable for astro-tourism mainly because it has:
o: Heavy industrial activity and bright urban lighting
Clear skies, least humidity and low pollution at high altitude
High humidity, dense cloud cover and low altitude
A warm marine climate and frequent rainfall
accepted.x: Hanle's clear skies, least humidity, low pollution and high altitude make Ladakh suitable for astro-tourism.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete favourable combination.
accepted.sec: Light pollution - dark sky reserves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Thermal pollution is most directly caused by:
o: Discharge of untreated domestic sewage alone
Reduction of artificial lighting in cities
Discharge of hot water from thermal and nuclear power plants and industries
accepted.x: Thermal and nuclear power plants use water as coolant, and industries may discharge hot water, causing thermal pollution.
accepted.tq: Identify the primary source rather than a general water-pollution source.
accepted.sec: Thermal pollution - sources, effect on DO  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Warmer water generally contains less dissolved oxygen.
Reason (R): The capacity of water to hold dissolved oxygen decreases as its temperature rises.

Select the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the reduced oxygen-holding capacity of warmer water directly explains why dissolved oxygen falls with increasing temperature.
accepted.tq: Check whether the scientific reason directly explains the asserted relationship.
accepted.sec: Thermal pollution - sources, effect on DO  [other exams]

accepted.s: Sudden changes in the temperature of a water body may:
o: Prevent all microbial activity in every case
Convert dissolved oxygen into nitrogen permanently
Improve the survival of all aquatic organisms
accepted.x: Sudden temperature changes can stress or kill aquatic life, while warmer water also holds less dissolved oxygen.
accepted.tq: Apply the thermal-stress effect to an aquatic situation.
accepted.sec: Thermal pollution - sources, effect on DO  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a measure for controlling thermal pollution?
accepted.x: Cooling towers, cooling ponds, recirculating cooling water and regulated discharge temperatures help control thermal pollution. Unregulated hot-water discharge worsens it.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated control measure.
accepted.sec: Thermal pollution - sources, effect on DO  [other exams]

accepted.s: Green mufflers used along roads generally consist of:
o: Rows of trees and shrubs that absorb noise
accepted.x: Green mufflers are rows of trees and shrubs along roads that help absorb noise.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a biological noise barrier from mechanical control devices.
accepted.sec: Noise control measures  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following as measures of noise control:
1. Traffic management
2. Proper maintenance of vehicles
3. Restrictions on loudspeakers
4. Zoning around hospitals and schools
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Traffic management, vehicle maintenance, loudspeaker limits and zoning around hospitals and schools are all stated noise-control measures.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete set of administrative and practical controls.
accepted.sec: Noise control measures  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The uranium mine and mill at Tummalapalle are operated by UCIL in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Tummalapalle uranium mine and mill of UCIL are located in YSR Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the exact location and operating organisation together.
accepted.sec: Tummalapalle uranium mining (AP)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following concerns has been alleged by villagers in relation to the Tummalapalle uranium mine and mill?
o: Improvement in groundwater quality near the tailings pond
Increased soil fertility due to uranium tailings
Groundwater contamination and skin or other health problems from the tailings pond
Reduction in all forms of industrial waste
accepted.x: Villagers have alleged groundwater contamination and skin or health problems associated with the tailings pond at Tummalapalle.
accepted.tq: Distinguish reported environmental and health concerns from their reversals.
accepted.sec: Tummalapalle uranium mining (AP)  [GROUP-II]
